llm.thesis: Intuit is a high-quality, capital-light compounder (13.9% TTM revenue growth, 27.4% operating margin +129bps YoY, 20% ROIC, 0.5x net debt/EBITDA, 8.8% shareholder yield) whose multiple has collapsed to the 0th percentile of its own five-year range — P/E 17x versus a 75x median, 8.8x P/FCF, 11.3% FCF yield — after a 59% twelve-month drawdown. That magnitude of de-rating in a business with no visible operating deterioration is not a multiple compression event; it is the market re-underwriting terminal value, almost certainly on the thesis that agentic AI commoditizes tax prep and SMB bookkeeping — the very theme (AI Software & Agents, trend 71) the engine scores as a tailwind. The investable question is therefore not 'is it cheap' (it demonstrably is on trailing numbers) but 'does the cash flow annuity survive'. Our read: Intuit owns the system of record, the filing rails and the proprietary financial data that an LLM cannot synthesize, which makes it more plausibly an AI distributor than an AI victim — but the market will not pay for that until reported net-new customer and ARPU data refute the disintermediation story. At 17x with a 7% buyback yield, we are being paid to wait, but the tape (price 29.6% below the 200-day, RSI 33, MACD negative, -22.5% in a month while Technology rotation runs +73) says do not anticipate the turn — scale in against evidence, not against valuation alone.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth is healthy but decelerating at the margin (13.9% TTM vs 15.1% prior), while profitability is still expanding: operating margin 27.4% (+129bps), EPS +20.4%, net income +18.0%, ROIC 20%. Cash generation is exceptional — $8.66B FCF on $21.4B revenue (40.4% margin) against just $175M capex — but 1.90x FCF conversion and +41.5% FCF growth are well above sustainable levels and likely flattered by working capital/deferred-revenue timing, so the 11.3% headline FCF yield should be haircut toward a normalized figure. Balance sheet is a non-issue (net debt/EBITDA 0.49x, interest coverage 23x), and capital return is real: $5.4B buybacks plus $1.35B dividends, share count -2.1%, though SBC at 9.6% of revenue absorbs a meaningful share of that repurchase.
llm.technical_read: The trend is decisively broken: price 286.8 sits below the 20- (326), 50- (325) and 200-day (407) averages, 29.6% under the 200-day and 59% off the 52-week high, with MACD histogram at -5.5. RSI 33 is oversold but not capitulatory, and the -22.5% one-month move after a +9.4% three-month bounce means the prior rally failed — a lower high followed by a fresh leg down. Structurally, reclaiming the 325-327 cluster (where the 20- and 50-day converge) would be the first genuine evidence of trend repair; until then any purchase is a knife-catch against a negative-relative-strength tape in an otherwise leading sector.
llm.market_expectation: At 17x earnings and ~9x free cash flow, versus 75x and 39x historical medians, the market is pricing an impairment of the franchise, not a slowdown: implicitly, that AI agents erode TurboTax and QuickBooks pricing power and that today's 27% operating margin and 14% growth converge toward low-single-digit growth with structurally lower economics. The PEG of 0.82 and the fact that capital is aggressively rotating into Technology (+73) while this name is down 22.5% in a month confirm the de-rating is idiosyncratic and narrative-driven, not macro or sector-driven. In short: the market is paying for none of the current earnings power and nothing for the AI optionality.
what_market_misses: The engine reports 'no flagged risks' — that is a coverage gap, not an all-clear. A 59% drawdown in a 20%-ROIC compounder with expanding margins is prima facie evidence of an unpriced structural narrative the quantitative checks do not capture; the honest framing is 'why is it cheap', not 'it is cheap'.

Intuit sits on the ownership side of the AI stack, not the disrupted side: it holds the system of record, the payroll/payments rails and decades of proprietary filing and SMB ledger data. An agent needs that data; the data does not need the agent. If AI collapses the cost to serve a customer, a 40% FCF margin business with $175M of capex converts that into margin, not price erosion.

Capital is rotating hard into Technology (+73, the only sector above +8) while INTU is making new relative lows. That divergence usually resolves violently in one direction — it is either the best risk/reward in the sector or the market's clearest tell that the business model is impaired. Position sizing should respect that binary.

The buyback is now a genuine compounding engine rather than a cosmetic offset: a 7.1% buyback yield executed at a 0th-percentile multiple retires far more value per dollar than the same $5.4B did at 75x earnings. Every quarter the price stays depressed mechanically raises forward per-share earnings.

Reported FCF quality is overstated at 1.90x conversion; a normalized ~1.2-1.4x conversion still leaves a high-single-digit FCF yield, which is the number to underwrite. Buying on the headline 11.3% is buying a timing artifact.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days after the 2026-09-09 filing): the single highest-information event — net-new customers, ARPU and consumer-segment retention will either confirm or refute the disintermediation narrative.
Evidence of AI monetization (agentic/assisted tiers driving ARPU rather than defending it), which would re-rate the multiple off the terminal-decline assumption.
Accelerated repurchase at depressed prices — buyback yield already 7.1%; upsizing would signal management's own view of intrinsic value.
Continued Technology rotation (+73) eventually pulling capital into the sector's most de-rated large-cap name once relative strength stabilizes.
A reclaim of the 325-327 area (20/50-day convergence) as technical confirmation that forced/momentum selling is exhausted.
risks: AI disintermediation of the core: LLM agents making tax filing and SMB bookkeeping near-free would compress both pricing and attach rates — this is the most plausible explanation for the 59% de-rating and is not disproven by trailing fundamentals.
Regulatory/competitive pressure on paid consumer tax filing (free-file alternatives) — a recurring structural overhang for this business model; treat as live until refuted by disclosed filer counts.
Valuation trap dynamics: trailing margins and ROIC are lagging indicators. A 0th-percentile multiple can persist for years if the market's terminal-growth assumption is right.
Technical/flow risk: 29.6% below the 200-day with negative MACD and a failed three-month bounce implies continued distribution; oversold can become more oversold.
Earnings quality: 9.6% SBC-to-revenue and 1.90x FCF conversion mean GAAP-adjusted, normalized owner earnings are materially below the headline FCF figure.
Revenue deceleration (13.9% vs 15.1%) turning into a step-down rather than a plateau, which would validate the bear case on the next print.
thesis_break_conditions: TTM revenue growth falls below 9% (currently 13.9%) or decelerates for two consecutive quarters.
Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY (currently 27.4%) — would signal pricing power loss rather than mix.
Management discloses declining paid customer counts or ARPU in the consumer tax or QuickBooks franchises — direct confirmation of AI/free-file disintermediation.
FCF conversion normalizes below ~1.0x alongside flat or falling absolute FCF, undermining the 11.3% yield anchor.
Buyback is cut or leverage rises materially above ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA (currently 0.49x).
Price fails to reclaim the 325-327 zone within two quarters while making new 52-week lows on rising volume.
Technology rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs, removing the sector tailwind.
Adverse regime (Stagflation + Contraction) probability exceeds 55% (currently ~48.6% combined).
second_order_beneficiaries: Hyperscalers and inference providers: Intuit's pivot to agentic experiences converts an asset-light $175M-capex model into a consumption buyer of GPU/inference capacity — the compute bill lands on cloud and model vendors regardless of whether Intuit wins or loses.
Foundation-model and AI tooling vendors: whoever supplies the reasoning layer captures spend from both Intuit's defensive build-out and from the challengers attacking it.

Payments and embedded-finance rails: if AI compresses the value of the software layer, monetization migrates to money movement (payroll, bill pay, lending) — the rails operators and sponsor banks capture that shift.
Financial data aggregators and open-banking infrastructure: agentic bookkeeping requires clean, permissioned bank/transaction data, a toll booth that profits whichever application layer wins.
Accounting and advisory services firms: if software commoditizes, the residual value migrates to human assurance and advisory relationships that agents cannot underwrite.
Cybersecurity and identity verification providers: automated filing and agent-initiated money movement raise fraud surface area, driving spend on identity and transaction-monitoring vendors.

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue $21.45B, +13.9% YoY, decelerating from +15.1%; operating margin 27.4% (+129bps); ROIC 20.0%; FCF $8.66B (40.4% margin).
P/E 16.8x vs 5y median 75x; EV/Sales 3.7x vs 12.2x median; P/FCF 8.8x vs 38.9x median — all at the 0th percentile of the five-year range.
Price -59.2% over 12 months, 59% below the 52-week high, 29.6% below the 200-day average, RSI 33, MACD histogram -5.5.
Net debt/EBITDA 0.49x, interest coverage 23x, buybacks $5.4B, diluted shares -2.1% YoY, SBC 9.6% of revenue.
Technology is the only sector with a strongly positive rotation score (+73) while this stock fell 22.5% in the last month.
The market is pricing a terminal impairment of the franchise rather than a cyclical slowdown, implying growth converging to low single digits and structurally lower margins.
The de-rating is idiosyncratic and narrative-driven rather than macro- or sector-driven, given the divergence from sector rotation.
1.90x FCF conversion and +41.5% FCF growth are flattered by working capital/deferred-revenue timing and should be normalized before underwriting the 11.3% FCF yield.
A 7.1% buyback yield executed at a 0th-percentile multiple is materially more value-accretive per dollar than historical repurchases at high multiples.
The engine's 'no flagged risks' output reflects incomplete coverage (estimate revisions, guidance and insider data not connected) rather than an absence of risk.
The drawdown is driven by fear that agentic AI commoditizes consumer tax prep and SMB bookkeeping, compressing pricing power.
Ownership of the system of record, filing rails and proprietary financial data makes Intuit a net distributor of AI rather than a victim, converting lower cost-to-serve into margin expansion.
Free-file and regulatory pressure on paid consumer tax filing is a live structural overhang contributing to the multiple compression.
